ownership.quote: Hostinger was founded in Kaunas in 2004 as Hosting Media. ... In 2011, Hosting Media renamed as Hostinger. ... In 2021, ConHostinger acquired a 31% stake in Hostinger.

stage.quote: In 2021, ConHostinger acquired a 31% stake in Hostinger.
stage.note: No VC seed/Series financing history was found for Hostinger; the company appears self-funded/bootstrapped since its 2004 founding and profitable (first EBITDA profit reported for 2023). The only outside-capital event found is a 2021 minority (31%) stake acquisition by a firm referred to as 'ConHostinger' (deal reported by CEE Legal Matters, partner named Thomas Strohe) — deal size, structure and whether it was primary/secondary capital were not confirmed within the research window (source page blocked by Cloudflare bot-check), so this is not classified as a priced VC round. Marked 'unknown' rather than 'bootstrapped' because a real minority stake sale to an outside investor did occur and its financing character could not be confirmed.

last_round.quote: In 2021, ConHostinger acquired a 31% stake in Hostinger.

revenue.basis: Company-reported figure (€275.4 million for FY2025) converted to USD at an approximate EUR/USD rate of ~1.08; press covered as company-sourced numbers, not a third-party estimate.
revenue.quote: Hostinger reported €275.4 million in revenue for 2025, up 51% year over year. ... The company reported its first EBITDA profit in 2023.

note: Hostinger is a Lithuanian (Kaunas-founded, Vilnius-headquartered) web hosting company operating since 2004, appears profitable and largely self-funded, with strong disclosed revenue growth (€69.6M in 2022 to €275.4M in 2025, ~58% CAGR, first EBITDA profit in 2023). One outside-capital event is documented — a 2021 acquisition of a 31% stake by an investor referred to as 'ConHostinger' (partner Thomas Strohe) — but deal terms (amount, whether it was a primary funding round or a secondary sale by early shareholders) could not be confirmed in the time available; the primary source (ceelegalmatters.com) was blocked by a bot-check. No YC/accelerator affiliation found. Its VPS product is a plain self-managed KVM VM line (see card), not an agent-native sandbox.
